claim_or_hypothesis: US-EU-Asia gas market cointegration strengthens or holds during acute crisis

claim_or_hypothesis: Oil-gas (HH-WTI) price-spread cointegration is a stable forecasting relationship
negative_or_contradictory_evidence: Price-spread and VECM models deliver accurate forecasts only until the cointegrating relationship breaks down (dated to Jan 2009 by formal test); post-break, these models perform WORSE than a random-walk benchmark (MSPE ratios up to 1.5), and a Markov-switching extension designed to detect the regime change in real time still fails to recover the pre-break performance
failure_mode: A once-reliable relationship became actively harmful to forecast accuracy after a structural break, and a regime-switching model built specifically to catch that break could not do so reliably in real time
pit_issue: PIT-clean result -- this is exactly the kind of finding real-time (as opposed to full-sample) evaluation is designed to catch
regime_dependency: High regime dependency -- textbook pre/post shale-gas-revolution structural break
recommended_disposition: reject any model design that assumes HH-WTI cointegration holds today, and treat this as a general warning against relying on any single historically-cointegrated relationship without an explicit, tested regime-break contingency
notes: Directly relevant to Commodity's PIT/backtest philosophy: this is the single cleanest documented example in the review of 'a relationship that worked in a full-sample backtest but would have actively hurt a real-time forecaster'

claim_or_hypothesis: Long-lag / highly parameterised VAR models improve natural-gas price forecasts
negative_or_contradictory_evidence: VAR(12) models on both the fundamentals-only and oil-augmented specifications UNDERPERFORM the random-walk benchmark at nearly every horizon (MSPE ratios above 1); parsimony (VAR(1)/BVAR(1)) combined with Bayesian shrinkage is required to beat the benchmark
failure_mode: Overfitting / over-parameterisation in a real-time forecasting setting
pit_issue: PIT-clean result (this is the paper's central real-time finding)
regime_dependency: Fairly stable finding across the whole sample (not just one regime)
recommended_disposition: reject complex/high-lag specifications as a default; prefer parsimonious models or explicit shrinkage, and require any complex model (ML/boosting/neural) to beat this documented parsimonious baseline out-of-sample before being preferred
notes: Directly relevant to Section 11's methodological scepticism requirement and to Commodity's own V1 result (HistGB RMSE 0.0465 vs naive RMSE 0.0453 -- i.e. the more complex model already underperformed the naive baseline in Commodity's own V1
